units.source: Naming software is hard. I lived in Ontario when I first started the project and Trillium (the flower) is sort of a provincial logo, many institutions in Ontario are named "Trillium [something]". So I kept hearing/reading it almost everyday, I liked the sound of it and its nature motif, so I just reused it.
units.context: FAQ > Inspiration for the name “Trilium”

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__– Zadam (original Trilium maintainer)__TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: FAQ > Inspiration for the name “Trilium”

units.source: Despite the fact that the Trillium flower has two “l"s, the Trilium application only has one.
units.context: FAQ > Inspiration for the name “Trilium”

units.source: Trilium has no separate folder type: any note can have child notes, so any note can act as a folder. A note can hold its own content and have children at the same time, unlike a file system, which separates files from directories.
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: To organize notes into a folder:
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: Create a note that acts as the folder, for example "Projects".
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: Right-click it in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__, or hover over it and press the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button.
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: To move existing notes into it, drag them onto it in the tree.
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: The children of a note are listed at the end of its content (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: If you want the note to look like a folder, with no content of its own and only its children shown, make it a collection instead: right-click in the tree, select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_3__, then choose __TRILIUM_PH_4__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__List View__TRILIUM_PH_7__. See __TRILIUM_PH_8__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_9__ for the other views, such as tables, boards and calendars.
units.context: FAQ > How do I create a folder?

units.source: Common request is to allow multiple users collaborate, share notes etc. So far I'm resisting this because of these reasons:
units.context: FAQ > Multi-user support

units.source: it's a huge feature, or rather a Pandora's box of collaboration features like user management, permissions, conflict resolution, real-time editing of a note by multiple people etc. This would be a huge amount of work. Trilium Notes is project made mostly by one person in free time and that's unlikely to change in the future.
units.context: FAQ > Multi-user support

units.source: given its size it would probably pivot the attention away from my main focus which is a personal note-taking
units.context: FAQ > Multi-user support

units.source: the assumption that only single person has access to the app simplifies many things, or just outright makes them possible. In multi-user app, our __TRILIUM_PH_0__scripting__TRILIUM_PH_1__support would be a XSS security hole, while with the single user assumption it's an endless customizable tool.
units.context: FAQ > Multi-user support

units.source: No.
units.context: FAQ > Can I use Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive to sync data across multiple computers.

units.source: These general purpose sync apps are not suitable to sync database files which are open and being worked on by another application. The result is that they will corrupt the database file, resulting in data loss and this message in the Trilium logs:
units.context: FAQ > Can I use Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive to sync data across multiple computers.

units.source: The only supported way to sync Trilium's data across the network is to use a __TRILIUM_PH_0__sync/web server__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: FAQ > Can I use Dropbox / Google Drive / OneDrive to sync data across multiple computers.

units.source: Trilium stores notes in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which is an SQLite database. People often ask why doesn't Trilium rather use flat files for note storage - it's fair question since flat files are easily interoperable, work with SCM/git etc.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Short answer is that file systems are simply not powerful enough for what we want to achieve with Trilium. Using filesystem would mean fewer features with probably more problems.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: More detailed answer:
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__clones__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are what you might call "hard directory link" in filesystem lingo, but this concept is not implemented in any filesystem
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: filesystems make a distinction between directory and file while there's intentionally no such difference in Trilium
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: files are stored in no particular order and user can't change this
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Trilium allows storing note __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which could be represented in extended user attributes but their support differs greatly among different filesystems / operating systems
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Trilium makes links / relations between different notes which can be quickly retrieved / navigated (e.g. for __TRILIUM_PH_0__note map__TRILIUM_PH_1__). There's no such support in file systems which means these would have to be stored in some kind of side-car files (mini-databases).
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Filesystems are generally not transactional. While this is not completely required for a note-taking application, having transactions make it way easier to keep notes and their metadata in predictable and consistent state.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > How can I search for notes when I'm not sure of the exact spelling?

units.source: Trilium places exact matches before fuzzy matches. When you search for "project", notes containing exactly "project" appear before notes with variations like "projects" or "projection", regardless of other scoring factors.
units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > Why do some search results appear before others with lower scores?

units.source: Use the "Fast search" option to search only titles and attributes (not content)
units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > How can I make my searches faster?

units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > How can I make my searches faster?

units.source: Set a result limit to prevent loading too many results
units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > How can I make my searches faster?

units.source: For large databases, consider archiving old notes to reduce search scope

units.source: Why does search sometimes find results with typos?__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > Why does search sometimes find results with typos?

units.source: Trilium uses a progressive search strategy that includes fuzzy matching when exact matches return fewer than 5 results. This finds notes despite minor typos in your search query. You can use fuzzy search operators (__TRILIUM_PH_0__ for fuzzy exact match and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ for fuzzy contains). See the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ documentation for details.
units.context: FAQ > Search-related Questions > Why does search sometimes find results with typos?
